assessment: This is an important study on the role of a bacterial cell wall component, D-alanylated lipoteichoic acid, as a cue in Drosophila melanogaster-microbiome interactions. Overall, the evidence presented to support the conclusions is compelling. The approach combines crystallography with biochemical and cellular assays that take advantage of both fly and bacterial mutants to demonstrate a physiological role in juvenile growth promotion. The work will be of broad interest to those studying host-microbe interactions, particularly aspects related to immunology and metabolism, mediated by the microbiome.
